name: Perform specialised reference tests
summary: Hospital laboratories and the company's own community laboratories refer specialised chemistry, endocrinology, therapeutic drug and toxicology tests to the reference laboratory. Technologists hold the specimens until each assay's scheduled batch, prepare and extract them by hand for mass spectrometry and chromatography or load them on specialised immunoassay analysers, review the data and QC, and release results after a second technologist's review and, for interpretive tests, a clinical scientist's comment. Turnaround is set mainly by the batch schedule, overnight instrument runs and review queues; low-volume assays need careful QC and a failed batch costs a whole rerun.

baseline.org_archetype: The reference laboratory of a large Canadian community laboratory company, serving more than 500 hospitals with specialised chemistry, endocrinology and toxicology testing.
baseline.notes: Starts when an accessioned referral specimen reaches the reference bench; referral intake, send-outs and result delivery are separate processes.

trigger: An accessioned referral specimen from hospital referral intake, or a specimen shipped from another company laboratory, arrives at the reference bench.
end_state: All reference tests on the requisition are released (with interpretive comments where needed) to hospital result delivery, a critical value is handed to the call desk, or the specimen is rejected and a new one requested.

volume.seasonality: Fairly even through the year; specialised testing is weekday-heavy and lower in late December.

evidence.note: From the organisation file process map (hospital referrals plus specialised community tests); seasonality is the author's estimate.

roles.title: Medical laboratory technologist, specialised chemistry and toxicology

evidence.note: Cost from the organisation file (Job Bank MLT times 1.35). About 55 of the 70 reference technologists work on this process; the rest is QC, maintenance, method work and proficiency testing; author's estimate.

roles.title: Laboratory assistant, referral accessioning and send-outs

evidence.note: Organisation file headcount 25, shared with referral accessioning and send-outs; about 10 FTE sort, store and retrieve specimens for the benches; author's estimate.
Second review of manual and mass spectrometry results, batch reruns and downtime; author's estimate within the eight charge technologists in the organisation file.
Delay notifications and downtime decisions; author's estimate.

roles.title: Laboratory medical director or clinical scientist (clinical pathologist, biochemist, microbiologist)
roles.department: Community laboratory testing (The model laboratory Laboratories)

evidence.note: Clinical scientists and biochemists interpret and comment on specialised results (f_hospital); FTE is the author's estimate.

Instrument middleware with autoverification and rerun rules

steps.name: Receive referred specimens at the reference bench
steps.description: A laboratory assistant takes accessioned referral specimens from intake or the inter-laboratory shipment, checks storage temperature on arrival (frozen, refrigerated or ambient), tube type and volume against the test's requirements, and matches each to the bench pending list.

error.defect_description: A specimen that thawed in transit is not noticed.

control.basis: ISO 15189 sample acceptance criteria (documented requirements for sample type, volume and transport temperature)

next.condition: wrong tube, thawed, short volume or unlabelled aliquot

evidence.note: Stability limits such as one week refrigerated and six months frozen (f_arup_vitd) drive the temperature check; the 3% problem share and times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Sort and store specimens until the scheduled run
steps.description: The assistant files each specimen in the freezer or refrigerator rack for its assay and run day, so that daily assays reach the bench the same day and weekly or twice-weekly assays wait for their batch.

error.defect_description: Specimen filed under the wrong assay or day.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Resolve an unsuitable specimen with the referring laboratory
steps.description: The charge technologist decides whether the specimen can be tested with a disclaimer or must be rejected, records the reason in the LIS and asks hospital client services to tell the referring laboratory and request a new specimen.

control.basis: ISO 15189 sample rejection and acceptance with disclaimer

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Build the batch worklist and pull specimens on run day
steps.description: On the assay's scheduled day the technologist prints the batch worklist from the LIS pending list, decides the run order with calibrators and controls, and pulls the specimens from storage; specimens arriving after the cut-off wait for the next batch.

error.defect_description: A pending specimen is left off the batch.

evidence.note: Batch schedules set turnaround (organisation file process map); daily immunoassays report within 24 hours while LC-MS/MS assays report in 1 to 5 days (f_arup_vitd, f_arup_testo). The wait range (one hour to five days) is the author's estimate for a mix of daily, twice-weekly and weekly assays.

steps.name: Thaw, aliquot and extract samples
steps.description: The technologist thaws and mixes the specimens, pipettes aliquots, and for mass spectrometry and chromatography assays adds internal standard and performs protein precipitation or solid-phase extraction before loading the plate; immunoassay samples are loaded directly with calibrators and controls.

error.defect_description: Pipetting or sample order error in the plate map.

control.basis: Validated examination procedure (ISO 15189 examination processes); calibration and QC run with each batch

evidence.note: LC-MS/MS method (f_arup_testo); hands-on time per requisition is the author's estimate for batches of about 40 to 90 samples.

steps.name: Run calibrators, controls and patient samples
steps.description: The instrument runs the batch, often overnight for mass spectrometry; nobody works on the samples during the run, which takes from under an hour for an immunoassay rack to many hours for a full LC-MS/MS plate.

evidence.note: Run times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Return specimens to storage
steps.description: The assistant returns primary tubes and remaining aliquots to the dated freezer or refrigerator racks so they can be found for repeats, add-ons and the retention period.

control.basis: ISO 15189 post-examination storage and retention of samples

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Process data and review chromatograms or curves
steps.description: The technologist opens the run in the instrument software, checks the calibration curve, internal standard recovery, ion ratios and retention times, corrects peak integration where needed, and transfers the results to the LIS through the middleware.

evidence.note: Specialised assays such as drug levels need manual handling and autoverify least often (f_krasowski); times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Accept the batch against QC rules
steps.description: The technologist checks the controls in the QC software against the multirule limits and the peer data and accepts or rejects the run; for low-volume assays with few QC points the decision leans on bracketing controls and recent calibration history.

control.basis: Westgard multirule QC and ISO 15189 quality control of examination results; results reported only from accepted runs

next.condition: run accepted; automated specialised immunoassay results pass rules
run accepted; manual, chromatography or flagged results need second review

evidence.note: QC rules from f_westgard; accreditation and proficiency testing required for licensed Ontario laboratories (f_ag2017, f_acd); the 4% rejection rate and the split between automated and second-review assays are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Technical review by a second technologist
steps.description: The charge technologist or a senior technologist reviews the results against the worklist, previous results for the patient, measuring range and plausibility (for example drug level against dose timing), and approves them or sends them for a repeat, a dilution, an alternate method or a clinical scientist.

control.basis: Laboratory procedure: second-person review of manual and mass spectrometry results

next.condition: interference suspected; confirm by another method

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Repeat or dilute in the next run
steps.description: The technologist retrieves the stored specimen, prepares a dilution or repeat extraction and adds it to the next scheduled batch; the result comes back through data review.

evidence.note: Repeat waits for the next batch of the assay; author's estimate.

steps.name: Clinical scientist interprets and comments
steps.description: The clinical biochemist or medical director reviews the result with the clinical details on the referral, writes an interpretive comment (for example on an electrophoresis pattern, an endocrine profile or a toxicology finding), and may recommend further tests or phone the referring laboratory.

control.basis: ISO 15189 interpretation of results by qualified personnel; laboratory director responsibility

next.condition: further testing on the stored specimen

evidence.note: Clinical pathologists and scientific leaders support clients (f_hospital); times and shares are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Release results in the LIS
steps.description: The technologist releases the approved results with any comments under their own login, which sends them to hospital result delivery or community reporting.

error.defect_description: Result released on the wrong requisition.

control.basis: Medical Laboratory Technology Act, 1991 scope of practice: results evaluated and released by a registered MLT

evidence.note: Time is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Confirm a critical value and hand it to the call desk
steps.description: For a result beyond a critical limit (for example a toxic lithium, digoxin or acetaminophen level), the technologist checks the specimen and dose timing, releases the result and puts it on the critical call list with the referring laboratory's contact so it is phoned at once.

error.defect_description: Critical queued with the wrong contact.

control.basis: OAML Guideline for Reporting Laboratory Test Results Level I drug and toxicology limits; ISO 15189 critical intervals

next.condition: critical handed to the call desk

evidence.note: Drug-level critical limits from f_oaml; delays at the reference laboratory hand-off (12 to 24 hours in one case) from f_cv2006.

steps.name: Confirm by an alternate method
steps.description: When an immunoassay result is implausible (suspected heterophile antibody, cross-reacting drug or metabolite), the technologist arranges a blocking-reagent treatment, dilution linearity study or a mass spectrometry confirmation in the next run.

next.condition: confirmation added to the next run

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Investigate a failed batch QC and recalibrate
steps.description: The technologist reviews the QC pattern, checks reagent and calibrator lots, internal standard response and recent maintenance, recalibrates or cleans the source, and documents the cause before asking to rerun the batch.

control.basis: CLSI C24 out-of-control procedure: find and correct the cause before patient testing resumes

evidence.note: Per-requisition time spreads the batch troubleshooting over its samples; author's estimate.

steps.name: Approve the batch rerun and log a nonconformance
steps.description: The charge technologist reviews the troubleshooting record, approves re-extraction and rerun of the batch in the next available slot, and logs the QC failure as a nonconformance.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of times.

steps.name: Log an instrument failure and salvage samples
steps.description: The charge technologist logs the failure in the maintenance system, calls the vendor's field service, checks which samples were injected and whether extracts can be re-injected, and plans the rerun.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Notify hospital clients of delayed results
steps.description: The reference laboratory manager approves overtime or a weekend run and asks hospital client services to tell referring laboratories which tests will be late and by how much.

control.basis: Client service agreement: notice of turnaround delays

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Rerun after repair and release with full review
steps.description: After the vendor repair and a passing calibration and QC, the technologist re-extracts or re-injects the samples, reviews every result and releases them.

control.basis: Patient testing resumes only after QC meets acceptance criteria (CLSI C24)

evidence.note: Wait covers vendor response and requalification; author's estimate.

exceptions.name: Unsuitable specimen
exceptions.description: Wrong tube, thawed specimen or short volume; tested with a disclaimer or rejected with a request for a new specimen.

exceptions.name: Failed batch QC
exceptions.description: The run's controls break a multirule limit; the batch is troubleshot, recalibrated, logged as a nonconformance and re-extracted in the next slot.

exceptions.name: Repeat, dilution or alternate method
exceptions.description: Over-range, implausible or interference-suspect results go to the next batch for a dilution, repeat or confirmation by another method.

exceptions.name: Instrument failure
exceptions.description: A mass spectrometer or analyser fails during a run; samples wait for field service and are rerun with full review, with delay notices to hospitals for long outages.

exceptions.name: Critical value
exceptions.description: A toxic drug level or other critical result is confirmed and handed to the results call desk.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from arrival at the reference bench to release of the last result
benchmarks.population: Specialised chemistry, endocrine, drug and toxicology referrals at a reference laboratory

evidence.note: Author's estimate for a mix of assays: daily immunoassays report within 24 hours (f_arup_vitd) and LC-MS/MS assays in 1 to 5 days (f_arup_testo) at a large US reference laboratory running seven days a week; a Canadian laboratory running some assays two or three times a week is assumed slower.

benchmarks.population: One large US reference laboratory (25-hydroxy and 1,25-dihydroxy vitamin D)

benchmarks.unit: billable tests per FTE per year
benchmarks.population: Lowest-volume chemistry, haematology and immunology peer group in a 151-institution Q-Probes study

evidence.note: Low-volume specialised work is less productive than high-volume core testing.

pain_points.description: Batch schedules mean a specimen arriving just after the cut-off waits days for the next run of its assay.

evidence.note: Turnaround of 1 to 5 days for LC-MS/MS even with daily runs.

pain_points.description: Manual extraction and chromatogram review make mass spectrometry assays labour-heavy and dependent on experienced technologists.

evidence.note: Drug levels need offline handling and autoverify least often.

pain_points.description: A failed QC run or instrument failure costs a full batch re-extraction and adds at least one batch cycle to every sample in it.
Second review and clinical scientist interpretation queue behind daytime availability.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

pain_points.description: Critical values found in batch testing reach the clinician through an extra hand-off from the referring hospital laboratory, which can add hours.

sources.title: Autoverification in a core clinical chemistry laboratory at an academic medical center (Krasowski et al.)
sources.supports: Drug levels (gentamicin, lithium, methotrexate) and serum free light chains autoverify least often, mainly because they need offline dilution and manual filing; all rules approved by the medical director.

sources.title: Westgard Rules: multirule QC
sources.supports: Multirule QC rejection rules (1-3s, 2-2s, R-4s, 4-1s, 10x); a run is rejected if any is violated.

sources.title: The 7 best practices to recover from an out-of-control event
sources.supports: CLSI C24-based steps: stop reporting, investigate root cause (calibration, reagent lot, maintenance), resume only after QC passes, re-analyse patient samples since the last acceptable QC, document and prevent recurrence.

assumptions: The assay mix is assumed to be about 45% specialised immunoassays that pass automated rules after an accepted run and 55% manual, chromatography or mass spectrometry results that get a second review.
Batch frequency ranges from daily to weekly; the batch wait (one hour to five days) is the main driver of elapsed time and is the author's estimate.
Instrument run time is waiting with zero hands-on time; batch-level work (worklist, QC acceptance, troubleshooting) is spread across the samples in the batch.
Send-outs and referral accessioning are separate processes; when a test cannot be done in-house it is sent out from intake, so this workflow has no send-out branch.
The lab_assistant_reference role is in the organisation file but not in the process map's role list for this process; it is used here for specimen sorting, storage and retrieval.
Critical results go to the company's results call desk, following the organisation file; for hospital referrals the call goes to the referring laboratory.
Critical values are about 0.3% of reference requisitions (about 180 a month), close to the 5% share of the organisation file's 2,500 monthly critical calls assumed in the critical result workflow.

Organisation file check: hands-on time times volume implies about 80 FTE, most of the reference laboratory's roughly 100 bench staff (70 technologists, 25 assistants, 8 charge technologists), leaving little for QC, maintenance, method validation and proficiency testing. The reference laboratory headcount may be low for 60,000 requisitions a month of largely manual specialised testing, or the requisition volume may be high.
Loaded costs come from the organisation file (hourly wage times 1.35).
